title: ws04-ws05-ws12-capability-core-tool-policy-wiring

test_results.outcome: all four packages ok (server 14.4s, policy cached, api 26.8s, cmd 10.5s)

residual_risks: With the switch off, decisions and signed evidence are unchanged: EvaluateTool runs the same gate, then DecideWithPolicies(riskResult, nil policies), which is the same as Decide(riskResult, binding). One thing does change: recordDecision now counts the post-binding result under the binding's side-effect class, where before it counted the raw riskResult under the capability's class. Only the PolicyDecisionsTotal metric labels move; decisions do not.

The PermissionDenied check on a person naming another user_id is not behind the switch. That matches the brief. Any non-service caller that sends someone else's user_id today will now be refused, even with TOOL_POLICY_ENFORCED off.
A person may still send an empty user_id. That skips their own user-scoped stored policies, but only ever with a weaker set: org policies still apply, and someone else's cannot be loaded.

When the switch is on and the policy store cannot be read, mapErr turns the wrapped DB error into codes.Internal with the raw error text. Fixing it needs a sentinel in engine.go, which is outside this packet. This must be handled before TOOL_POLICY_ENFORCED goes on.

execution-core (runtime_loop/mod.rs near line 760) labels any policy_source other than approval_floor as a high-risk pause, so a tool_policy_ask pause shows the wrong cause. This is a follow-up before enabling.
No cmd/ wiring test was added. The brief allowed skipping it when there is no seam.

capabilities.pb.go is LF in the working copy (git warns it would become CRLF), and docker-compose.yml is also LF. Both were kept LF, matching the files as they were. main.go, server.go and the proto are consistently CRLF.
deploy_notes: Enabling this needs TOOL_POLICY_ENFORCED=true in the deploy env, which is off by default. Before turning it on: (1) execution-core labels any policy_source other than approval_floor as a high-risk pause (apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/runtime_loop/mod.rs around line 760), so tool_policy_ask pauses show the wrong cause; (2) a failed policy-store read reaches callers as codes.Internal with the raw DB error text, because mapErr defaults unknown errors that way; a sentinel mapped to Unavailable needs engine.go, which is outside this packet. The PermissionDenied caller check is not switch-gated, so a person asserting another user_id is refused even with the switch off; the person path still allows an empty user_id, which skips that person's own stored policies. The packet's file list was used even though the task text said (none); the packet said docker-compose.yml and capabilities.pb.go are CRLF, but both are LF in this worktree and were kept LF.
summary: Wired stored per-tool policies into capability-core EvaluatePolicy and main, switch default off. cmd/main.go builds api.NewToolPoliciesHandler(pool), passes it with ToolPolicyEnforcedFromLookup(os.Getenv) to policy.New(...).WithToolPolicies, mounts its routes on protectedMux, and logs the enforced flag once at boot. server.go EvaluatePolicy now uses verifiedPrincipal, refuses a non-service caller naming another user_id with PermissionDenied before any policy read, and calls s.policy.EvaluateTool in place of EvaluateCapability plus Decide; earlier returns are unchanged. With the switch off, EvaluateTool reduces to the same riskResult then Decide path, so decisions and evidence match. Added TOOL_POLICY_ENFORCED (default false) to the capability-core compose block, and updated the policy_source comment in the proto and in the generated pb.go (comment only). New test file covers: switch off ignores a stored never and never reads the store; switch on applies never and ask with the source in response and evidence; person naming another user gets PermissionDenied and nothing is read, self and service pass. Status: edits and new test file are in place and gofmt-clean where applicable; go vet and go test were started in the background but had produced no output when I stopped, so they are NOT confirmed. Nothing committed.

title: ws04-ws05-ws12-gateway-grant-fallback-and-probe-scope
residual_risks: The plan_approval call to clear_grant (http_routes.rs, guarded by durable_grant && durably_recorded) has no test of its own. Only PlanModeStore::clear_grant is unit-tested. If the call were dropped, a stale narrower memory copy would shadow a later successful approval on the same replica, and no test would catch it.

clear_grant only clears the replica that took the later approval. Suppose a narrow approval fails on replica A and a broader approval later succeeds on replica B. A keeps honouring its narrower copy until that copy expires (up to 24 h). This errs toward the narrower rung, so it is safe, but a user can see an approval come out narrower than expected on A.

mp_contracts::autonomy::rank gives Unspecified and ReadOnly the same rank. So a memory copy of either one ties with a durable ReadOnly, and Session Core's grant is kept. That is correct per the brief, but it relies on the order rank defines.
The size-ratchet gate was already over its ceiling for sse.rs and http_routes.rs before this change. This change adds lines to both (+38 and +96).
deploy_notes: Nothing committed; the lead commits. Not run: the integration tests under apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/tests, notably tests/run_control_two_replica_test.rs, which exercises the peer receipts path, and anything outside the four --lib filters in the packet. The lead may want those run before the commit. No docker, no git write commands, and no .env files read. The new tests are in-process (LoopbackHub and fake persist closures), so none needs DATABASE_URL.
summary: Implemented both halves of packet ws04-ws05-ws12-gateway-grant-fallback-and-probe-scope (rows D1-026 and D1-463), touching only the five files the packet lists. A) D1-026: with_local_fallback in sse.rs now returns the narrower of Session Core's grant and this replica's in-memory copy (mp_contracts::autonomy::rank). A tie keeps Session Core's grant unchanged. The read_failed passthrough and the no-grant fallback are unchanged. When the memory copy wins, its rung, peek_approved_plan and grant_expires_at are used, and the log line carries ids and rung labels only. Added PlanModeStore::clear_grant(org_id, thread_id) in coordinator.rs, which removes the entry only when its org matches. plan_approval in http_routes.rs calls it right after durably_recorded is computed, guarded by durable_grant && durably_recorded. B) D1-463: RunControlReply gained an optional conversation_only (serde default, skipped when None; PROTOCOL_VERSION unchanged). The owner's probe answer fills it from QueuedInputRegistry::stream_for. StreamThread::Peer now carries { thread_id, conversation_only: Option<bool> }. queue_input_with_receipts uses the known scope when Some and keeps the guess-and-retry only when None, meaning an owner that predates the field. Switches default off: with_local_fallback and clear_grant run only under the durable grant switch, the probe field is additive and skipped when None, and the receipts path is unchanged when its switch is off. No message text or bearer goes on the bus (ids and a bool only). ZDR gate untouched. grpc.rs not touched. Line endings preserved per file (sse.rs, http_routes.rs and run_control.rs are LF; coordinator.rs and queued_input.rs are CRLF). Discrepancy: the task text listed the editable files as (none), but the packet's files array names these five, and I followed the packet. Size ratchet: sse.rs grew 20888 to 20926 lines (+38) and http_routes.rs grew 15028 to 15124 (+96). Both were already above their recorded ceilings in scripts/gates/baselines/file-size.json (sse.rs 19664, http_routes.rs 12533) before this change, so that gate was already failing on those files.
